clue.text: Deadly sin taking hold of old diplomat

indicators.note: the sin grips the next piece, so it is placed inside that word

parts.note: envy is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A sinful old diplomat in the grip of covetousness.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a diplomatic representative sent on a mission.

clue.text: Greek dramatist sheds tear for men observing Furies

indicators.note: sheds means drops, so the following piece is taken out
for means in exchange, so the men piece takes its place

parts.note: Euripides was an Athenian tragic playwright
a rip is a tear
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient playwright weeps for the men watching avenging spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheds tear for men' swaps RIP out of EURIPIDES and MEN in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eumenides, 'kindly ones', is a euphemistic Greek name for the Furies.

clue.text: Meeting-place unused, say, after victory in Europe

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the other

parts.note: VE as in VE Day, Victory in Europe

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: something unused is new

explanation.surface: A place for meeting, unused since the war ended in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is the place where an event or gathering is held.

clue.text: Youngster with strong desire to change first name

indicators.note: the first instance of the following letter is replaced

parts.note: a yearning is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A child longing to be called something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say what N becomes; the crossing letters show it is L.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is an animal in its second year, a young one.

clue.text: Trendy bloke promises to pay? That's crafty

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
Sid is a stock name for any ordinary man
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A fashionable man who hands out IOUs is up to something sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Insidious describes something treacherously cunning, proceeding subtly to do harm.

clue.text: Piece of information for partners

definitions.meaning: an entry in a list or news report
a couple in a romantic relationship, as in 'they are a couple'

explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single detail or piece of news, and also a romantically linked couple.

clue.text: Hi-fi fanatic's received idea?

definitions.meaning: a fixed, oversimplified notion widely accepted

explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is a conventional, oversimplified image; split, it is a kind of stereo buff.

clue.text: Put in clear water filled with fish

indicators.note: the river contains the fish, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Putting a fish into clear water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' is the opposite of code here, and 'water' is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a coded message is to translate it into plain language, or 'clear'.

clue.text: Healer manipulated toes, given work at hospital

indicators.note: manipulated means handled and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A healer working in hospital who manipulated someone's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats ailments by manipulating bones and muscles.

clue.text: Emblem of authority the general's assistants recognised

definitions.meaning: a rod or baton carried as a symbol of office
the officers who help a commander run an army

explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a ceremonial rod of office, and also the officers serving a commander.

clue.text: Moroccan extremists shortly identify this steel component

definitions.text: Moroccan extremists shortly identify this steel component

parts.words: Moroccan extremists shortly identify this steel component
parts.note: the outer letters of Moroccan are M and N, and Mn is the chemical symbol (a short form) for the metal added to steel

explanation.surface: Moroccan radicals are named briefly as part of a steel-making story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' looks political but means the first and last letters; 'shortly' says those letters are the element's abbreviated symbol, which is how they identify it.
explanation.definitionFit: This metallic element is alloyed with iron to make steel harder and tougher.

clue.text: Church garment regarded as excessive in California

indicators.note: the excess sits within the state's abbreviation

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: A vestment thought too much by Californian standards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short surplice worn by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: Pointer with one eye?

parts.note: a sharp sewing implement comes to a point and has a single eye for the thread, though the surface suggests a one-eyed dog

explanation.definitionFit: A sewing needle is pointed at one end and pierced by a single eye at the other.

clue.text: Forestalls threatened fate of Queen of Hearts' gardeners

definitions.meaning: to forestall is to intercept and prevent something in advance

definitions.text: threatened fate of Queen of Hearts' gardeners
definitions.meaning: in Alice in Wonderland the Queen of Hearts orders the gardeners who painted her roses to be beheaded

explanation.definitionFit: To head off is to intercept and prevent; literally, beheadings were the queen's threat to the gardeners.

clue.text: Bug giving fruit-picker throat irritation at first

indicators.note: at first says this piece comes before the other

parts.note: a frog in the throat is hoarseness
a hopper picks hops, the fruit of the hop plant

explanation.surface: An insect bothering a harvester with a sore throat.
explanation.walkthrough: Hop-picking was a traditional British seasonal job.
explanation.definitionFit: A froghopper is a small jumping insect, a true bug whose nymphs make cuckoo spit.

clue.text: Corrupt type always in time to suppress information

indicators.note: the always-piece is placed within the time-word

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down, so this word is kept inside the other

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A bad lot who forever hides the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested containers: the information sits inside 'always', and that pair sits inside 'time'. E'ER is the poetic spelling of ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A degenerate is a person regarded as morally depraved or debased.

clue.text: Dick enters southern state? Incautious to do so uninvited

indicators.note: enters means comes in next, so this piece follows

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, a southern US state
dick and tec are both slang for a detective
rash means incautious

explanation.surface: A detective arrives in the Deep South, warned it is reckless to turn up unasked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to do so' points back to 'enters', so the definition is to enter uninvited.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to go into a party or event without an invitation.

clue.text: Nag pettily, parking at end of estate?

parts.note: in the phrase estate car, the word that ends it is car
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Complaining about where the car is left at the edge of a housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of estate' looks like a letter pick but means the word that follows estate in 'estate car', the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault or complain about trivial matters.

clue.text: Traveller not contributing to other people's efforts?

definitions.text: not contributing to other people's efforts?
definitions.meaning: a member of a team who does no work and is carried by the others

explanation.definitionFit: A passenger rides in a vehicle, and figuratively is a team member who contributes nothing.

clue.text: They relieve pain somehow? Yes and no

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asked whether painkillers work, the answer is yes and no.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodynes are painkilling medicines.

clue.text: Verse that features this son of Adam

indicators.note: features says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A line of scripture that mentions one of Adam's sons.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth is named in Genesis as the third son of Adam and Eve.

clue.text: Plant displaying a cleft article in this way

parts.note: a cleft is a split or gap
an is the indefinite article
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: A plant that shows a split piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Agapanthus is a flowering plant, the African lily, with blue or white blooms.

clue.text: Attack a number of ships positioned around Spithead

indicators.note: the fleet word is placed around the single letter

parts.note: sail is used as a collective for ships, as in 'twenty sail'
read as Spit-head, the head of spit is its first letter

explanation.surface: Ships massed around Spithead, the anchorage off Portsmouth, to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Spithead is a naval anchorage off Portsmouth in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently.

clue.text: Not involved with races, one is up a tree

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps out of the races and climbs a tree instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' signals the anagram of NOT and RACES; the tree is a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear appears higher up a family tree than the people descended from them.

clue.text: Ultimately lacking time to finish travel book

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the following letter is taken away

parts.note: ultimately means at last

explanation.surface: Short of time to finish a travel book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to finish' says the T removed is the final one of AT LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps, used for planning travel.

clue.text: Like English fish taken by the French, hopefully

definitions.text: Like English fish taken by the French, hopefully

indicators.note: taken by means attached to, so these letters follow on

parts.note: to dib is to fish by bobbing the bait on the water
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A dig at French gourmets hoping to make something of English seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs onto a second column of the page. Read whole, it says what one hopes of English fish served up to the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Something edible is fit to be eaten, which is what any cook hopes the dish will be.

clue.text: Reportedly hostile reaction to drink

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: boos are a hostile reaction from a crowd

explanation.surface: Rumours of an angry response to alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal for alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Infant born in aircraft compartment

indicators.note: the born letter goes inside the compartment

parts.note: a bay, as in bomb bay, is a compartment in an aircraft

explanation.surface: A baby born mid-flight in the hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name a newborn or very young child not yet walking or talking.

clue.text: Security device rejected by a climber

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nail fastens and secures things

explanation.surface: A climber turning down the safety gear on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine that climbs up trees in tropical forests.

clue.text: Performing with no end of joy, lad goes in for church music

indicators.note: the lad piece goes inside the shortened word
with no says the following letter is taken away

parts.note: performing on an instrument is playing

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the following word

parts.note: a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: A joyless boy sings in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The lad piece lands inside the shortened word just before its last letter G, splitting it as PLAIN plus G.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied medieval chant used in church services.

clue.text: Erudite note about church written by Lear's uncle

indicators.note: written by means placed beside, so these letters follow
the note goes round the church abbreviation

parts.note: sol is a note of the sol-fa scale
Edward Lear wrote the nonsense poem Incidents in the Life of My Uncle Arly

explanation.surface: A learned note about a church, penned by a relative of Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear here is the nonsense poet Edward Lear, not the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarly means learned or erudite, showing academic knowledge.

clue.text: Direct movement of sword, finally changing side

indicators.note: the last letter, standing for left, swaps to the letter standing for right

parts.note: steel is a poetic word for a sword

explanation.surface: A fencer's blade swinging round to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R are the abbreviations for left and right, the two sides.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide or control the course of something.
